alt.en: An engraved page of music numbered 430, headed "Comin thro' the rye. 1st Sett." and "Written for this Work by Robert Burns.", number 417, marked Very Slow, with four systems of voice and bass, the words "Comin thro' the rye, poor body" and "Jenny's a' weet poor body" under the notes, and two short verses below.
alt.es: Página de música grabada con el número 430, con el encabezado "Comin thro' the rye. 1st Sett." y "Written for this Work by Robert Burns.", número 417, marcada Very Slow, con cuatro sistemas de voz y bajo, la letra "Comin thro' the rye, poor body" y "Jenny's a' weet poor body" bajo las notas y dos estrofas cortas debajo.

caption.en: Burns's first set of the song, No. 417 of The Scots Musical Museum, volume 5 (1796), with the old chorus about Jenny's soaked petticoat, here in the volume's 1839 Edinburgh reissue, which heads it "Written for this Work by Robert Burns".
caption.es: La primera versión de Burns, el n.º 417 del quinto volumen de The Scots Musical Museum (1796), con el viejo estribillo de la enagua empapada de Jenny, aquí en la reedición del volumen hecha en Edimburgo en 1839, que la encabeza con "Written for this Work by Robert Burns".

source: The Scotish Musical Museum, vol. 5 (Edinburgh: William Blackwood and Sons; London: Thomas Cadell, 1839), originally published by James Johnson; p. 430, No. 417, "Comin thro' the rye. 1st Sett"

alt.en: An engraved page of music numbered 431, headed "Comin thro' the rye. 2d Sett.", number 418, marked Very Slow, with four systems of voice and bass, the words "Gin a body meet a body, Comin thro' the rye" and "Ilka body has a body" under the notes, and two more verses below.
alt.es: Página de música grabada con el número 431, con el encabezado "Comin thro' the rye. 2d Sett.", número 418, marcada Very Slow, con cuatro sistemas de voz y bajo, la letra "Gin a body meet a body, Comin thro' the rye" e "Ilka body has a body" bajo las notas y dos estrofas más debajo.

caption.en: No. 418, the unsigned second set in the same volume (1796), the "Ilka body has a body" version that became the popular song, here in the 1839 Edinburgh reissue.
caption.es: El n.º 418, la segunda versión, sin firma, del mismo volumen (1796), la de "Ilka body has a body" que se hizo popular, aquí en la reedición de Edimburgo de 1839.

source: The Scotish Musical Museum, vol. 5 (Edinburgh: William Blackwood and Sons; London: Thomas Cadell, 1839), originally published by James Johnson; p. 431, No. 418, "Comin thro' the rye. 2d Sett" (cropped above No. 419)

alt.en: A yellowed engraved page of dance music numbered 41, headed in script "The Millers Wedding" and "Strathspey", with four systems of a melody over a bass line, no words, and "Number 6" at the foot.
alt.es: Página amarillenta de música de danza grabada, con el número 41, con el encabezado manuscrito "The Millers Wedding" y "Strathspey", con cuatro sistemas de una melodía sobre una línea de bajo, sin letra, y "Number 6" al pie.

caption.en: The Miller's Wedding, the strathspey to which Dick and Glen trace this song's tune, on page 41 of A Collection of Scots Reels or Country Dances as Preston and Sons sold it in London about 1790; Robert Bremner had printed the tune in his collection of reels in 1759.
caption.es: The Miller's Wedding, el strathspey al que Dick y Glen remontan la melodía de esta canción, en la página 41 de A Collection of Scots Reels or Country Dances tal como la vendía Preston and Sons en Londres hacia 1790; Robert Bremner había impreso la melodía en su colección de reels de 1759.

source: A Collection of Scots Reels or Country Dances, with a Bass for the Violoncello or Harpsichord (London: Printed and sold by Preston and Sons, no. 97 Strand; dated 1790 from the British Library catalogue), p. 41, "The Millers Wedding: Strathspey"

alt.en: A printed page of music numbered 10, headed "Comin' thro' the rye." and "Arranged by T. M. Mudie", marked Moderato with a metronome mark of 72, with a voice line over a piano part, the words of the first verse under the notes, and a footnote: "Often sung 'greet.'"
alt.es: Página de música impresa con el número 10, con el encabezado "Comin' thro' the rye." y "Arranged by T. M. Mudie", marcada Moderato con una indicación de metrónomo de 72, con una línea de voz sobre una parte de piano, la letra de la primera estrofa bajo las notas y una nota al pie: "Often sung 'greet.'"

caption.en: The second set as G. F. Graham printed it in The Songs of Scotland, volume 2 (Edinburgh, 1848; some copies are dated 1849), with T. M. Mudie's piano part and the words and tune our arrangement follows.
caption.es: La segunda versión tal como la imprimió G. F. Graham en The Songs of Scotland, volumen 2 (Edimburgo, 1848; algunos ejemplares llevan la fecha de 1849), con el piano de T. M. Mudie y la letra y la melodía que sigue nuestro arreglo.

source: G. F. Graham, The Songs of Scotland, adapted to their appropriate melodies, vol. 2 (Edinburgh: Wood and Co., 1848; three volumes bound in one), p. 10, "Comin' thro' the rye", arranged by T. M. Mudie
